arm_b_infeasibility_note: A real finding, not a bug, if n_arm_b_infeasible > 0 -- ARM B (uniform-r ToMe) applies a merge operation at 11 SEPARATE blocks, paying this device's near-fixed per-merge-operation overhead 11 times over, vs ARM A/TANDEM's own <=2-point schedule concentrating the same token reduction into 1-2 operations. At tight budgets this can make even the smallest uniform-r candidate (r=1) cost more than the budget allows. See per-row arm_b_infeasible in frontier_plans.csv.
d_pred_note: ARM B's D_pred is null in frontier_plans.csv -- P2.1's own Dm_table.csv only covers TANDEM's registered plan-space grid (MERGE_BLOCKS x MERGE_RS, 24 rows), not ARM B's uniform-every-block r in {1..11}. See this file's module docstring D_PRED NOTE. The real comparison is measured top-1 accuracy via frontier_paired_eval.py.
not_a_joint_vs_staged_test_note: This is NOT a joint-vs-staged test -- that comparison is VOID on this device/LUT, see CHARACTERIZATION.md. This compares merge-PLACEMENT granularity (TANDEM's own <=2-point schedules, ARM A) against uniform-r merging (ARM B) at matched measured latency -- the hardware analogue of the P2.2 saturation finding.
